memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, 'But my brother Esau is a hairy man while I have smooth skin. What if my father touches me? I would appear to be tricking him and would bring down a curse on myself rather than a blessing.' His mother said to him, 'My son, let the curse fall on me. Just do what I say; go and get them for me.'" - Gen 27:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob hesitates — but notice what worries him. He does not say, "Mother, this is wrong; we would be lying to my blind old father." His only concern is, "What if I get caught?" He fears the curse of being exposed, not the sin itself. His conscience is troubled by the risk, not by the wrongdoing.

That is a revealing moment, and an honest mirror for us. It is possible to hesitate over a sin only because we are afraid of consequences, not because we love what is right. We may avoid a wrong thing simply because we might get caught — and that is not the same as hating the wrong.

Rebekah's reply is even more startling: "Let the curse fall on me." She is so set on her plan that she is willing to gamble with a curse to push it through. This is what happens when we are determined to have our own way — we start bargaining recklessly, brushing aside every warning.

May God give us a deeper conscience — one that shrinks from sin because it grieves Him, not merely because we might be found out. True integrity does the right thing even when no one would ever know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I avoid sin because I love what is right, or only because I fear getting caught?
2. Where am I bargaining recklessly to get my own way?
3. What would change if I hated sin the way God does?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a tender conscience that turns from sin because it grieves You, not merely because I fear being caught. Make me a person of true integrity. Amen.
